newsitem.title: FRANCE: French evacuate 100 safely from Albania.
newsitem.headline: French evacuate 100 safely from Albania.

text.p: France safely evacuated about 100 people aboard four military helicopters from chaos-torn Albania to Italy on Friday, the French Foreign Ministry said.
The helicopters embarked the evacuees in the port of Durres and flew them to Brindisi, a ministry spokesman told Reuters.
"About half were French nationals and the others were from other countries," he said.

Foreign Minister Herve de Charette, accompanying President Jacques Chirac on a Latin America tour, was returning specially to attend a meeting this weekend of European Union foreign ministers in the Netherlands expected to deal mostly with Albania, the spokesman added.
The armed forces earlier said the French helicopters would evacuate 72 people including several Romanians, ex-Yugoslavs, Italians and Albanian spouses of French nationals.
Two of the helicopters arrived in Durres from Brindisi and two from a French base in ex-Yugoslavia, the spokesman said.
The French operation took place as the United States, Italy and Britain evacuated hundreds of foreigners from Albania by air and sea as the tiny Balkan country slid further towards anarchy.

Some 10 French diplomats and diplomatic service employees remain at the embassy in Tirana, the Foreign Ministry spokesman said. There are also nearly a dozen French journalists in the country, he added.
